title: NAB sees RBA hike supporting AUD near term, but the medium-term risk points the other way
body: The message for the Australian dollar is two-sided. A hike today, and any hint of a November follow-up, would support the currency in the near term, but NAB's argument implies the rate premium Australia now holds over other G10 markets could erode if traders begin pricing earlier RBA easing than at its peers. With a 25bp hike close to fully priced, the reaction is likely to hinge on the statement and Governor Bullock's press conference, in particular whether the board keeps November open. AUD/USD has been trading around 0.70, with US dollar strength and higher Treasury yields already a headwind. --- Earlier RBA preview: 25bp hike to 4.60% widely expected as sticky inflation lingers Sticky core inflation pushes RBA towards its highest cash rate since 2011 RBA preview: A 25 bps rate hike is priced in, but what comes after that? All four major Australian banks now forecast RBA hike to 4.60% on September 29 RBA governor Bullock flags inflation risks as higher neutral rates come into focus RBA's Bullock says supply shocks hard for policy to manage, flags second round risk RBA's Hunter says rates may need to rise again as inflation risks stay tilted higher --- NAB argues the RBA's next hikes may lift the Australian dollar near term, but leave Australia as one of the first G10 economies forced to reverse course. Summary: The RBA is expected to raise the cash rate by 25bp to 4.60% today, and NAB sees a meaningful risk of another increase in November.

title: Weak Treasury auctions and Fed hike bets push US 10-year yield to highest since June 2007
body: Yields at these levels tighten financial conditions across mortgages, corporate debt and equity valuations, and analysts have said a sustained move above 5.2% would likely keep the US dollar supported while pressuring gold and risk assets. The S&P 500 has so far held within a few percent of its record high, so a further rise in real yields is a test of that resilience. Borrowing costs are already feeling it, with the average 30-year US mortgage rate at around 7.1%, its highest in more than two years. Oil has rebounded on Iran headlines, but the message from the bond market is that supply and Fed policy, not energy, are now the dominant drivers. --- Treasury yields are climbing on real yields and weak auction demand rather than inflation expectations, leaving the 10-year above 5.2% as markets price a likely October Fed hike. Summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5.2% on Monday, its highest since June 2007, while the 30-year yield has reached around 5.5%, its highest since 2004. A senior US economist at Aberdeen said the rise is driven by real yields rather than inflation expectations, noting the two-year breakeven has barely moved this week and remains well below earlier highs. The economist said markets are reacting to weak Treasury auction demand and signs of an accelerating US economy, which are raising expectations of tighter Fed policy.

title: More from Araqchi: Iran hopes for final US reply via Qatar by Tuesday
body: The reference to a Tuesday timeline gives oil traders a near-term catalyst, which concentrates headline risk into the next day or so. Language that mediation has become more serious is modestly constructive for those pricing a Hormuz reopening, though Tehran has not detailed its conditions and Washington has publicly disputed the idea of sanctions relief, so the signal is mixed. Crude has been trading in both directions on each diplomatic headline, and that is likely to continue until a US reply either narrows or widens the gaps on sequencing. --- Earlier: Araqchi: Iran discussed ideas with Qatari mediators, Hormuz conditions must be met Trump denies offering Iran sanctions relief, calls Axios report a hoax ---Iran says mediation through Qatar and Pakistan has turned more serious since it presented a plan, and it wants the US final answer by Tuesday. Summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said he hopes to receive the US final response through Qatari mediators by Tuesday, according to IRNA. He said Tehran discussed with the Qatari mediators ideas on how to fulfil Iran's conditions, and that the mediators will raise those ideas with the US side. Araqchi said the Qatari and Pakistani mediation channels have taken a more serious form after Iran presented a plan. The remarks follow earlier comments that the US response will be relayed through Qatar and that the Supreme Leader's conditions must be implemented for the Strait of Hormuz to reopen.

title: OpenAI scraps GPT-6.1 Astra release over safety concerns, WSJ reports
body: A rare decision by a major developer to withhold a finished model may prompt fresh questions about the pace of frontier AI releases and how much safety work could slow the industry's roadmap. It could also temper expectations around new product announcements at OpenAI's developer conference, though the report gives no indication of a direct hit to AI infrastructure spending. Sentiment towards AI-linked stocks may be sensitive to any sign that agent safety incidents become a broader constraint on deployment. Competitors, including Anthropic, are named as having urged the industry to slow down and invest in safety standards, which suggests the caution is not confined to one company. --- More tech info here from earlier: ICYMI: Nvidia lifts buyback by record $150 billion to $235 billion, shares rise Technical analysis: Nvidia record buyback lifts shares, $232-$234 resistance a hurdle for now --- OpenAI is shelving a more capable model because it showed higher deception and overreached on tasks, a rare safety-driven retreat on the eve of its developer conference. title: Araqchi: Iran discussed ideas with Qatari mediators, Hormuz conditions must be met
body: The remarks suggest the Qatari mediation channel is live, but they also show Iran tying any Hormuz reopening to conditions it has not spelled out, which keeps a supply risk premium in oil. Crude has been trading in both directions on each new diplomatic headline, and firm language from Tehran could limit downside if traders had been leaning on the earlier reports of possible sanctions relief. The next catalyst is the US reply, which will be relayed through Qatar, so any sign of movement on sequencing, or a breakdown, is likely to drive the next leg in Brent and WTI. --- Earlier: Trump denies offering Iran sanctions relief, calls Axios report a hoax --- Iran is keeping the diplomatic door open through Qatar while insisting the Supreme Leader's conditions must be met before the Strait of Hormuz reopens. Summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran discussed ideas with Qatari mediators that are to be put to the US, according to IRNA. He said the US response will be conveyed to Tehran through the Qatari mediators. Araqchi said the conditions stressed by Iran's Supreme Leader must be implemented for the Strait of Hormuz to reopen. He added that if the US wants an agreement or a peaceful solution, Iran has already presented one. The comments follow Trump's rejection of Iran's Hormuz proposal on Saturday and a disputed Axios report on possible US sanctions relief.

title: Trump denies offering Iran sanctions relief, calls Axios report a hoax
body: The denial adds another layer of uncertainty to a crude market that has been trading almost entirely on Iran diplomacy headlines. Market reports noted that the original relief reports coincided with softer oil, a slightly weaker US dollar and gains in Treasuries, equities and gold, so a flat denial risks unwinding some of that repricing. The counterweight is that price reactions to Trump's social media posts on the war have been shrinking, according to Axios reporting in August, which may limit the move. For oil, the direction of travel still depends on whether mediated talks make progress on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and on whether conflicting official messaging keeps a risk premium in the market. --- Trump's flat denial leaves markets with conflicting signals on Iran sanctions relief just as mediators prepare to bring both sides back to the table. Summary: Trump posted on Truth Social that an Axios story saying he offered Iran sanctions relief and frozen funds was untrue, saying he offered "nothing," and demanded that Axios withdraw it immediately. Axios, citing US officials, had reported that Trump is willing to provide sanctions relief and release frozen Iranian funds in return for concrete Iranian steps on the nuclear program. CNN carried similar remarks from a US official.

title: Oil Rises as US-Iran Uncertainty Persists
body: Crude oil rose above $93 per barrel on Tuesday, extending its recent gains as persistent uncertainty over US-Iran negotiations outweighed the impact of resumed flows through Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. Iranian officials have reportedly downplayed the likelihood of a deal to end hostilities in the Middle East and reopen the Strait of Hormuz before the US midterm elections in November. Recent talks between the US and Iran in New York yielded limited progress, with President Donald Trump rejecting Tehran's latest proposal to reopen the strategic shipping lane. Even so, Trump is said to be weighing potential sanctions relief for Iran and the unfreezing of assets if there is meaningful movement toward a new nuclear agreement. At the same time, Saudi Arabia has reportedly restored oil flows to about 3.5 million barrels per day after repairing a key pipeline that offers an alternative export route bypassing Hormuz. title: UK Shop Price Inflation Slows in September
body: UK shop price inflation eased to 1.4% year-on-year in September 2026, down from 1.5% in August and slightly below market expectations of 1.5%. Despite the slowdown, it remained above the three-month average of 1.3%. Food price inflation fell to 2.5% from 2.8%, supported by promotions that reduced the cost of meat and dairy. However, poor harvests in Europe pushed up fruit prices, while elevated commodity costs kept chocolate and confectionery prices high. Non-food inflation also edged down, slipping to 0.8% from 0.9%, as heavy discounting lowered the prices of back-to-school essentials. The British Retail Consortium noted that retailers are continuing to absorb higher business rates, employment costs, energy bills and packaging taxes, but cautioned that there is a limit to how much additional cost pressure businesses can bear. In contrast, the UK's broader CPI inflation rate rose to 3.1% in August and is projected to exceed 4% in early 2027, driven by higher energy prices linked to the war in Iran. title: UK Shop Price Inflation Slows Again as BRC Index Eases to 1.4% in September
body: Annual shop price inflation in the United Kingdom edged down in September 2026, with the BRC Shop Price Index easing to 1.4% year-over-year from 1.5% in the previous month. The latest reading, updated on 28 September 2026, signals a further moderation in price pressures on the high street. The index measures the year-over-year change in shop prices, comparing the price level in September 2026 with that of September 2025. The prior figure compared August 2026 prices with those of August 2025. The slight deceleration suggests that while prices are still rising compared with a year earlier, the pace of increase continues to cool, offering some relief to consumers and potentially easing pressure on retailers navigating a still-cautious spending environment. title: Irish Consumer Confidence Dips in September, Signalling Softer Sentiment
body: Consumer confidence in Ireland weakened in September 2026, as the headline indicator slipped to 61.1 from 63.2 in August 2026, according to the latest data updated on 28 September 2026. The decline suggests Irish households are becoming slightly more cautious in their outlook for the economy and their personal finances. While the drop is modest, the move lower may indicate rising uncertainty among consumers heading into the final quarter of the year. A softer confidence reading often points to potential restraint in household spending, a key driver of domestic economic activity. Analysts and market participants will be watching subsequent releases closely to assess whether September's decline marks the start of a broader downtrend in sentiment or a short-term pullback within an otherwise stable confidence environment. title: New Zealand Stocks Track Wall Street Lower
body: The NZX 50 slipped 76 points, or 0.6%, to 13,755 in Tuesday morning trade, snapping the gains made in the previous session and mirroring an overnight decline on Wall Street. The drop followed a jump in US Treasury yields, as rising oil prices rekindled inflation concerns and strengthened expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike. Investors were also positioning ahead of a series of key data releases this week, including New Zealand's September business confidence figures, China's PMI data, and the US PCE Index and labour market reports, all of which could influence the Fed's policy stance at its upcoming meeting. The benchmark index fell to its lowest level since 18 September, with energy, real estate, and utilities shares exerting the most downward pressure. Notable early decliners included Freightways Group (-1.9%), Channel Infrastructure (-1.7%), South Port NZ (-1.2%), Briscoe Group (-0.9%), Mercury NZ (-0.8%), Mainfreight (-0.5%), and ANZ Group (-0.5%). In contrast, Hallenstein Glasson rose 4.6% after reporting a 49.9% jump in net profit for the year ended 1 August 2026. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Jamaica Raises Policy Rate to 6%
body: At its September 2026 meeting, Jamaica's central bank raised its policy rate by 50 basis points to 6.0%, responding to persistent inflationary pressures, higher commodity prices, and elevated geopolitical risks that are clouding the economic outlook. The bank emphasized that inflation risks remain tilted to the upside. Headline inflation rose to 7.9% in August from 7.5% in July, staying above the target range for a third straight month, while core inflation was unchanged at 5.2%. Policymakers expect inflation to increase further in the near term before gradually returning to the target range by mid-2027. Drought conditions and a strengthening El Niño are projected to keep agricultural prices high, and rising global commodity prices are feeding through to higher fuel, energy, and transport costs. In addition, post-disaster recovery spending following Hurricane Melissa could further add to price pressures. Businesses' 12‑month inflation expectations climbed to 7.3% in July from 6.7% in June. title: South Korea Manufacturing Sentiment Weakens
body: South Korea's manufacturing Business Survey Index (BSI) declined to 79 points in September 2026, down from 81 in July, signaling a continued weakening in business conditions. The production index slipped to 89 from 92, and the new orders index dropped to 87 from 92, underscoring softer demand and output. In contrast, the inventories index climbed to 103 from 100, suggesting a buildup of stock, while the financial situation index edged down to 81 from 82, indicating a slight deterioration in firms' financial health. Overall, the manufacturing Composite Business Sentiment Index fell by 4.3 points to 99.5 in September, and the outlook index for the following month declined by 1.4 points to 101.1, both reflecting a worsening in business sentiment. title: Ibovespa Falls as Oil Rally Resumes
body: The Ibovespa slipped 0.3% on Monday, closing at 182,991, pressured by a weak external backdrop, higher inflation expectations, and fresh polling that confirmed a tight presidential race. Oil prices resumed their advance after US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, reigniting concerns that energy-driven inflation could keep interest rates higher for longer. Rising bond yields weighed on credit-sensitive shares, dragging down major banks, with Itaú and Bradesco each losing 1%. On the macro front, the BCB's Focus survey showed that market participants raised their 2026 inflation forecast from 4.92% to 4.99%, while the year-end 2026 Selic rate projection was unchanged at 13.5%. Politically, a new election poll indicated that President Lula has widened his lead over Flávio Bolsonaro, who is regarded by markets as the more fiscally conservative candidate in a context of elevated domestic yields and sluggish business activity. Among individual names, Ambev (-0.8%), WEG (-1.9%) and Vivo (-2%) were notable underperformers. In contrast, Petrobras climbed 1.5%, while Vale advanced 0.5%. title: TSX Falls Amid Oil Rebound
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index fell 0.9% to close at 35,490, as a renewed surge in oil prices reignited inflation concerns. Crude extended its rally after US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, heightening fears that energy-driven inflation shocks could force interest rates to remain elevated for longer. Bond yields climbed in response, weighing on rate-sensitive sectors. Financials declined, with both CIBC and National Bank slipping 1%. Weakness in precious metals also dragged on the broader market, as lower gold prices hit mining stocks: Agnico Eagle dropped 5.1%, Barrick fell 4.1%, and WPM lost 5%. By contrast, energy producers benefited from the rebound in crude, with Cenovus gaining 0.7% and Suncor advancing 0.9%. Looking ahead, Tuesday's Canadian GDP release will be closely watched for signs of underlying economic momentum and for guidance on the Bank of Canada's next policy moves. title: US Stocks Slide as Bond Selloff Deepens
body: US stock indices finished lower on Monday as escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran drove fresh volatility in the oil market and weighed on bonds. The S&P 500 slipped 0.8%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 347 points, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 1.1%. The renewed rally in crude prices heightened worries that stronger inflationary pressures could force the Federal Reserve to deliver additional interest-rate hikes. Bond selling accelerated after President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to its highest level in 19 years. Investors are now focused on this week's PCE inflation data and the monthly jobs report, which are expected to offer further clarity on the strength of the US economy and the Fed's likely policy trajectory. Tighter financial conditions continued to weigh on AI hyperscalers and semiconductor manufacturers, many of which are tapping debt markets at record levels. Among the megacaps, Microsoft declined 1.3%, Amazon fell 1.4%, and Meta dropped 4.8%. In the chip sector, Micron slid 2.6%, AMD lost 3.6%, and Intel sank 5.7%.
